scope: read-only research on BITBLTBUF DBW zero and indexed DBW one; no emulator, console, or game execution

manual.title: GS Users Manual, Version 6.0
manual.manual_terms_note: The mirrored PDF labels itself SCE Confidential and restricts distribution/use to licensed developers and publishers. This receipt stores no PDF or page image and only paraphrases the relevant constraints.

source_facts.printed_page_101_bitbltbuf: SBW/DBW are pixel-width counts in units of 64 pixels; footnote gives the allowed range 1..32. Therefore DBW=0 is invalid/out of specification. The passage does not state what hardware does for zero.
source_facts.section_2_6_texture_buffer: Texture-buffer width is a 64-texel multiple generally and a 128-texel multiple for PSMT8/PSMT4. This is a separate texture-buffer constraint; it does not make BITBLTBUF DBW=1 numerically invalid.
source_facts.section_8_5_address_unit_correction: SBP/DBP/TBP values count 64-word (256-byte) blocks, not 256-bit units. No DBW=0 or indexed DBW=1 page-row stride rule was found in the manual sections reviewed.

claims.claim: BITBLTBUF DBW is width in units of pixels/64 and permitted range is 1..32.
Manual excerpt does not specify the GS response to DBW=0.
claims.note: absence claim needs human review; do not treat as verified hardware behavior

claims.claim: Texture buffer width for PSMT8/PSMT4 must be a multiple of 128 texels.
DBW=1 is within BITBLTBUF numeric range, while TBW=1 violates the indexed texture-buffer width constraint.

hardware_test_repository.limits: Repository README describes tests run on PS2 with expected results, but the inspected GS tests do not probe DBW. Absence in this pinned tree is not evidence of chip behavior or that no such tests exist elsewhere.

software_model_comparison.source: Parent's synthetic software-only probes; not hardware evidence
software_model_comparison.pcsx2: raw zero DBW divided by indexed page width produces zero rows; pinned GS width/page helpers use BW as supplied
software_model_comparison.ps2recomp: some standalone indexed helpers clamp page rows to at least one; actual CPU upload backend separately clamps DBW to max(DBW,1), yielding stride zero for indexed DBW 0/1 in the traced profile
software_model_comparison.resolution: Neither software behavior establishes silicon behavior. The manual makes DBW=0 invalid, and does not specify recovery behavior. Indexed DBW=1 is a valid BITBLTBUF field value but is not compliant as a PSMT8/PSMT4 texture-buffer width; a transfer-only use is not resolved by that texture-buffer restriction.
